header: IN THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH AT KARACHI.
Date Order with Signature of Judge
Appellant Muhammad Amir alias Raja produced in custody in Cr.Jail Appeal No.31/08.
Appellant Muhammad Farman produced in custody in Cr. Jail Appeal No.32 of 2008.
Z.K. Arif Advocate for the State.
body: ABDUL RAHMAN FARUQ PIRZADA ;- By this single judgment I propose to dispose of two Cr. Jail Appeals viz:- Cr. J.A.No.31/2008 on behalf of appellant/convict Muhammad Amir alias Raja and Cr. Jail Appeal No.32/2008 on behalf of appellant/convict Muhammad Farman, as both the appeals pertain to same case. Both the appellants were convicted and sentenced by impugned judgment dated 10.08.2006 passed by learned Vth Additional Sessions Judge, Karachi South in Sessions Case No.48/2004 vide Crime No.282/2003, P.S Gizri, Karachi South U/S 395, 109, 412 PPC, and sentenced to undergo R.I for seven years and to pay fine of Rs.50,000/= each and in case of default they shall undergo R.I for further one year more; the benefit of Section 382-B Cr.P.C was extended to the accused; the amount of fine if realized was to be deposited in the Government Treasury. Co-accused Liaquat Ali and Fakhar were convicted and sentenced to two years R.I and to pay fine of Rs.5000/= each and in failure to pay fine they had to undergo R.I for six months more. Co-accused Mst. Asia was convicted U/S 109 PPC, but was sentenced to the period already undergone during trial, while co-accused Mst. Mumtaz was acquitted.

2. Both the appellants produced in custody have submitted that they have already remained in jail since January 2004, and have faced rigorous imprisonment for major period of the sentence awarded to them. Their appeals were apparently time barred, for which both of them have stated that they genuinely intended to engage their counsel for filing their appeals, but due to extreme poverty they could not engage any private counsel, as such apparent delay occurred in filing the jail appeals. They have submitted that the delay in filing appeals was not deliberate, but was due to sufficient and natural cause. The report and jail roll in respect of both the appeals were called from Superintendent Central Prison, Karachi. By his report dated 03.05.2008, the Superintendent has stated that the delay which occurred in filing the jail appeals by appellants, was not intentional, but was due to reason that they had intended to engage their private counsel, but since they were unable to do so due to their poverty, as such subsequently the jail appeals were filed. The Superintendent himself has prayed that the period of delay in filing jail appeals may be condoned and the appeals be admitted for regular hearing. The learned State counsel also fairly conceded to this proposition, in view of the attending circumstances. Accordingly the delay in filing the jail appeals is hereby condoned and the appeals are decided according to law.

3. As per Jail Roll submitted by Superintendent Central Prison Karachi, out of the total sentence with fine viz:- 8 years, the un-expired portion of sentence of appellants comes to three years and four months after excluding the remissions earned by them.

4. It has been stated that the co-accused Waseem Shahzad and Muhammad Ali had filed Criminal Appeals No.314/2006 and 324/06, respectively before this Court and through the common judgment by this Court, their appeals were dismissed with the modification that their sentences awarded by learned trial court were reduced to the period of three years and six months and fine of Rs. 25,000/= and in case of default in payment of fine they shall suffer R.I for six months more.

5. Both the appellants at the very outset, have prayed for the modification in the sentences awarded to them, to the effect that their sentences may be reduced to the period of three years and six months and fine of Rs.25,000/=, as in the case of co-accused their sentences were reduced to the said period.

6. Learned state counsel has fairly opined that the impugned judgment in respect of appeals may be modified, in accordance with the judgment of this Court passed in the appeals of co-accused Waseem Shahzad and Muhammad Ali.

7. Considering the merits of the case, prima-facie the case of appellants stands virtually on the same footings as that of the Waseem Shahzad & Muhammad Ali. Accordingly their appeals are dismissed, with the modification to the extent that the sentences awarded to them by learned trial court vide impugned judgment, are reduced to the period of three years and six months and fine of Rs.25,000/=, and in case of default in payment of fine they shall suffer imprisonment for six months more.
8. With the above observation and modification in sentences of appellants, these appeals are disposed of.
